title: Centralize staging head and receipt authentication construction
evidence: Six preparation paths repeat receipt-key/ordinal construction, a provisional head with placeholder selected-receipt digest, head digest, make_receipt, receipt reference and final head reconstruction. The source optionality, lifecycle and custody election differ; the digest construction order is identical.

staging/integrity.rs:121-181 constructs all 18 receipt fields twice solely to attach the computed digest. staging/digest.rs:90-122 reconstructs all 18 fields again to zero the last digest before hashing the encoded prefix that excludes that very field.

Focused codec confirmation: codec/staging_progress.rs:343-385 encodes the receipt fields then encodes its digest as the final 32 bytes; canonical_staging_progress_bytes simply calls that encoder. The digest field has no effect on the hashed prefix.

Conversation-history design's staging contract explicitly defines the one-way head/receipt digest construction and separately authenticated selected receipt. Atomic-batch and draft_mutation_staging tests exercise independent wrong-page/receipt/head bytes, ordinal overflow and source/target custody.
proposal: Have one private authenticated staging-transition constructor derive the provisional/final head and receipt from explicit source/begin, target lanes/lifecycle and closed command evidence, returning the same separate records. Preserve all command-specific admission/terminal/custody checks. Borrow the original receipt for prefix hashing and add a narrowly scoped internal digest attachment operation to avoid full receipt reconstruction; retain unrestricted codec/fault construction where malformed-record tests require it.
required_contract_changes: None if both persisted records, selected receipt key, hash domains, prefix framing and exact canonical bytes remain identical. Do not merge head and receipt, replace equality with digest equality, infer terminal evidence, or widen public proof constructors.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Consolidate six 40-60-line digest/finalization sequences with one approximately 65-90-line helper and explicit small call-site arguments, including adapters and byte/digest fixtures. About 25-35 additional net lines come from eliminating digest-only receipt reconstruction; those are included in this total.
estimated_net_lines.overlap: Staging-only construction and staging receipt digest. Excludes DT-002 draft-piece build receipt digest work, DP-001 build creation, SA admission sealing, public staging-model accessors and independent canonical test encoders.

verification: Old/new canonical bytes and digests for begin, both lanes, finish, transfer and every terminal evidence shape, including ordinal-one terminal-before-begin.
Keep selected-key commitment independent from selected-receipt digest, malformed natural identity/tag cases, noncanonical and occupied-byte cases and checked ordinal/total overflow.
Keep atomic 257-page admission, post-finish 256-page/fragment and 65,536 inserted-byte ceilings, 14+2*pages acquisition bound, partial-prefix rejection, replay and all actual writer cuts.
confidence: high on exact digest redundancy; medium-high on shared transition helper

Ordinary build/status authentication must also prove published and hidden active marker roots; transactional authentication runs on a DomainReader and has different error mapping.

staging/acquisition.rs enforces read and encoded-value budgets before acquisition; mod.rs fixed limits and maximum-window tests make these observable. Replacing the paths with an unmetered generic reader or scanning released pages would violate authority.

Terminal-before-begin Conflict has None-to-None custody and immutable observed same-session evidence; admitted terminalization permits only Rejected/Cancelled/Error with Staging-to-None. Builder settlement owns terminal outcomes after transfer. Distinct evidence variants are not interchangeable errors.

Persisted keys and values deliberately repeat identity; independently durable head/receipt, build/fragment endpoints, canonical bytes and immediate predecessor proofs detect missing, ahead, occupied or mismatched records. All associated model/codec-facing constructors and public getters were examined.

test_unadmitted_marker.rs is an explicit cfg-limited test-only authorization registry, not an alternative production marker-admission API. Durable marker suites intentionally use it to create independent malformed or unadmitted inputs.
proposal: Retain the bounded authentication, independent records, closed evidence variants and test-only capability boundary. Any future common reader must preserve metering and exact error/custody semantics and demonstrate actual net benefit; no such generalization is counted here.
required_contract_changes: Deleting independent receipt/head authority, reconstructing from caller pages, collapsing terminal classes or bypassing acquisition accounting would require incompatible system/schema changes and is rejected under current authority.

title: Bracket candidate-session closure reads with the mutable head observations
evidence: session.rs:673-705 reads first and second session heads consecutively at 681-682, returns ConcurrentChange if they differ, and only then reads the natural closure at 691. There is no final head observation.

Focused supporting source: syndic-storage/src/read.rs:570-584 delegates every point to HomeStore::read_point; beryl-home-store/src/read.rs:396-413 creates a fresh database snapshot for each point call. The composite read does not share one snapshot.

Concrete valid interleaving: both initial reads capture session H selecting build/staging endpoint n; a normal admitted page/fragment advance commits endpoint n+1 and its session successor; active_operation_custody_is_exact (session.rs:288-373) reads the new endpoint and compares it to H's old custody. It returns false, so the public read reports InvariantFailure although the observed head changed during closure acquisition.

Authority: syndic-storage/doc/design-mutation-protocols.md:94-107 requires mutable anchors first and last and distinguishes drift from a missing/disagreeing closure under a stable anchor. Conversation-history design:1169-1173 and1216-1218 requires mutable wrappers to stabilize the selected session/pair rather than combine selections. The API already has ConcurrentChange.

Statically demonstrated interleaving only; no concurrency reproduction, build or test was run. Existing examined tests cover stable corrupted closure and serial mutation races, not this between-point-read schedule.
proposal: Read the named session head, acquire its bounded natural-closure result, then re-read the same head before classifying that result. Return ConcurrentChange on head drift; only a stable head permits Active/Disposed or InvariantFailure classification. Keep absence/wrong-kind and read-failure handling explicit and bounded; do not introduce an unbounded retry loop.
required_contract_changes: No new product or persistence contract; this restores existing stabilization/error-classification intent. A deterministic read interleaving hook or shared bounded snapshot approach must be selected during implementation. Retain stable corruption as InvariantFailure and real storage errors as errors.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Correctness issue, not a simplification saving; implementation and deterministic regression coverage may add lines.
estimated_net_lines.overlap: Independent from DP-003 immutable identity predicate. Does not claim every staging status/reconciliation path has been fixed by this one change.

verification: Deterministically pause after the second current head read, commit a valid staging page, build fragment or settlement successor, then resume closure reads; expected ConcurrentChange.
Keep stable missing selected receipt, ahead build, substituted history and disposed-receipt corruption classified as InvariantFailure.
Verify bounded read count and no retry spin; normal stable active/disposed/absent behavior remains unchanged.
confidence: high on ordering defect and valid interleaving; runtime reproduction not performed
